rows.practice: reads major philosophers in their own texts, puts forward an argument with a sense of what makes it sound and weighs the strong and weak points on each side of a question
rows.knowledge: some core theories and arguments across epistemology, logic, metaphysics or mind and across ethics, political or social philosophy
rows.identity: a philosopher in training who examines the values and ethics beneath society and own life, reflects on own progress and academic integrity and compares views across cultures and traditions

rows.practice: builds subtle, rigorous arguments along original lines, interprets texts across periods and traditions and uses philosophy to clarify real ethical dilemmas
rows.knowledge: a systematic, comparative command of theoretical and practical philosophy and of the debates over philosophical method, at times reaching beyond what was taught
rows.identity: an intellectually honest philosopher who suspends judgement, meets new perspectives with curiosity and revises even firm convictions when the argument demands it

rows.practice: conceives and completes an extended philosophical research project that contributes to the field, building and testing demanding arguments and texts with rigorous method
rows.knowledge: specialist expertise in at least one area or tradition, a thorough grasp of the discipline's debates shaped by current research and a reflective sense of philosophy's own methods and assumptions
rows.identity: a philosopher who reasons ethically, sees how philosophy can help address moral, social and political problems and keeps growing as a philosopher through independent study

digest.definition: Concerned with how we make sense of the world, of ourselves and of our relations; seen as underpinning the other disciplines and as sitting where the humanities and the social and natural sciences meet
distinctiveFeatures: Concerned with how we make sense of the world, of ourselves and of our relations; seen as underpinning the other disciplines and as sitting where the humanities and the social and natural sciences meet
Asks the large questions of knowledge, value, existence, morality and social life, with a clarifying role that supports constructive dialogue

Pluralistic: analytic, continental and comparative traditions, world philosophies among them, with methods from formal and logical analysis to hermeneutics, conceptual engineering and phenomenology; the traditions share precision, clarity and self-reflection
Learned by doing: students practise philosophy rather than only study a body of knowledge, through reading, discussion and presentation, and formal methods through graded exercises
Seeks a safe space for controversial and uncomfortable views, voiced with care and met constructively, and a community of enquiry that values every member
Acknowledges a past canon dominated by privileged European men and treats diversifying the curriculum as imperative
Often studied jointly with other subjects, and taught by philosophers inside other disciplines' accredited degrees

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: named Equity, diversity and inclusion: limited access to the subject before university; varied materials, activities and assessment; a safe but challenging space for controversial views; diversifying a narrow Western canon; the Equality Act 2010 and the Public Sector Equality Duty; outward-looking comparison of traditions; reflective logs (D1, 1.5 to 1.12); assessment variety as an EDI gain from GenAI (D1, 1.31); bringing diverse students together (D1, 3.13)

named Accessibility and the needs of disabled students: an anticipatory approach after the Disabled Students Commission report (clear expectations, care that asynchronous materials and automated captions do not create new barriers, multiple means of engagement); reasonable adjustments; audio and audiovisual resources; the insight disabled students bring to debate (D1, 1.13 to 1.16); alternative assessments (D1, 3.18)

named Education for sustainable development: sustainability defined as a moral attribute of acts, processes and institutions; the UN SDGs and the 2021 Advance HE and QAA guidance; philosophy as critique of the concept and as a resource for exposing false sustainability claims (D1, 1.17 to 1.19); sustainability among the concepts other professions' degrees teach (D1, 2.6)

named Employability, enterprise and entrepreneurship education: clear thinking, logic and argument as employability skills; joint programmes, placements and years abroad; assessments such as policy briefs; support for social enterprise; leadership strengths; the sectors graduates enter (D1, 1.20 to 1.27)

named Generative artificial intelligence: weighed against the degree's principal skills; formative benefits (critiquing outputs, an interlocutor, help for reticent students); risks to reading, analysis and originality; a challenge to essay-based assessment and integrity; GenAI as a philosophical topic in its own right (D1, 1.28 to 1.33)

transferable.text: You will be able to spot the issues, questions and problems a topic raises.
You will be able to see what you do not yet know and go and learn it.
You will be able to understand and analyse the knowledge and information you come across.
You will be able to pull together what is currently known about a topic.
You will be able to use what you know to reach conclusions backed by evidence.
You will be able to communicate well and appropriately, in speech or in other forms.
You will be able to set out what you know, or an argument, so other people can follow it.
You will be able to use different digital tools critically to gather, analyse, choose and present information.
You will be able to think for yourself: work on your own with the right support, carry out your own research and make critical judgements.
You will be able to work with others, in a group or team or by joining in discussions.
You will be able to reflect on your own progress, including how you keep your work honest and properly referenced.
You will be able to recognise and question the values and ethics behind culture, society and your own life.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Philosophy degree
Equity, diversity and inclusion: Increasing awareness and understanding

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject
statements.about: comparing perspectives across cultures and traditions
statements.paraphrase: Philosophical discussion flourishes when it looks outward; teachers bring views from other cultures and traditions into materials and discussion; graduates should be skilled at comparing and judging such views; courses use varied tools so every student is heard.

forPractitioner.text: Bring views from other cultures and traditions into materials and discussion, since graduates should be skilled at comparing and judging them; use varied tools and strategies so that every student can speak and contribute.

forBeneficiary.text: You should become skilled at comparing and weighing up philosophical views from different cultures and traditions.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Philosophy degree

statements.appliesTo: course teams in the subject
statements.about: the 2021 ESD guidance as a core resource
statements.paraphrase: The statement follows the UN Sustainable Development Goals and their priorities on climate, ecosystems, oceans, settlements, poverty and inclusion; the subject fits the skills and outcomes of the 2021 Advance HE and QAA guidance on education for sustainable development, which course teams should consult as a core resource.

forPractitioner.text: Use the Advance HE and QAA guidance on education for sustainable development (March 2021) as a core resource when you design the course; the subject aligns with its skills and outcomes, read against the UN Sustainable Development Goals.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team to consult a guidance document; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Philosophy degree

statements.appliesTo: joint and combined honours students
statements.about: joint honours students reach the core skills
statements.paraphrase: Students taking philosophy in a combined or joint degree, major and minor routes included, will reach the core of the subject-specific and generic skills the statement sets out and will add others from their other subject; they may also explore where the disciplines overlap.

forPractitioner.text: Joint and combined honours students will achieve the core subject-specific and generic skills of the statement and add skills from their other subject; plan chances for them to work across the overlap.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study philosophy alongside another subject, you will gain the core philosophical and general skills described here, add skills from your other subject and may explore where the two meet.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Philosophy degree

statements.appliesTo: providers of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Externality is a core part of UK quality assurance; providers will bring in external reviewers during periodic review for an independent view of planned changes and to confirm that threshold standards are met and the content fits the subject.

forPractitioner.text: In periodic review, providers will involve external reviewers, who give an independent view on proposed changes and check that threshold standards are reached and the content suits philosophy.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in course review

statements.appliesTo: anyone studying or teaching the subject
statements.about: traditions not to be assumed opposed
statements.paraphrase: Philosophy has many traditions, each with its own style and concerns, yet all share features such as precision, clarity and self-reflection; it should not be taken for granted that the traditions are at odds or unable to talk to each other.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the traditions as distinct but compatible: share their common stress on precision, clarity and self-reflection, and do not assume they are at odds or cannot engage productively.

forBeneficiary.text: You should not assume that different philosophical traditions are opposed or cannot learn from each other; they share a concern with precision, clarity and self-reflection.

statements.appliesTo: teaching and learning in the subject
statements.paraphrase: Programmes build the skills to do philosophy, not only to study it, so it matters that teaching models philosophical practice; time for gaining knowledge of topics and thinkers must be balanced with time in which students discuss, analyse and work out their own responses.

forPractitioner.text: Model the practice of philosophy in teaching: time spent acquiring knowledge of topics and thinkers must be balanced with time in which students discuss, analyse and work out their own responses.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course in how teaching is balanced; the student meets its effect

statements.appliesTo: every programme in the subject
statements.about: student-led research, peer exchange and self-direction
statements.paraphrase: Programmes differ in size, so the mix of online and in-person teaching and the range of topics vary; all programmes will nonetheless include some student-led research, chances to exchange ideas with peers and freedom for students to choose the questions they pursue.

forPractitioner.text: Whatever its size, every programme will include student-led research, peer exchange of ideas and room for students to direct the questions they pursue.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the programme; the student meets its effect as research, discussion and choice

headingPath: Teaching and learning: Learning in Philosophy is progressive

statements.appliesTo: teaching in the subject
statements.about: bringing students of different backgrounds together
statements.paraphrase: Many departments teach some subjects in a two-year cycle, with difficulty rising towards the final years; because philosophy draws on diverse thinkers, teaching strategies will involve gathering students from different backgrounds around shared problems, and it is important to offer varied modes of discussion, online or in person.

forPractitioner.text: Teaching strategies will bring students from different backgrounds together to work on shared problems; offer several modes and occasions for discussion, online and in person, so everyone can take part.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in teaching strategy

statements.appliesTo: the assessment suite of every programme
statements.paraphrase: Each programme's set of assessments will test students' knowledge and understanding, balanced against their competence in philosophical skills and methods.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure the suite of assessments will test knowledge and understanding, alongside philosophical skills and methods.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the programme in designing assessment

statements.appliesTo: the assessment suite of every programme
statements.paraphrase: Each programme's assessments will test argument and analysis: reasoning with rigour, critically, creatively and independently.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure the suite of assessments will test argument and analysis, showing rigorous, critical, creative and independent reasoning.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the programme in designing assessment

statements.appliesTo: the assessment suite of every programme
statements.paraphrase: Each programme's assessments will test presentation: getting ideas across clearly, reliably and effectively.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure the suite of assessments will test presentation: clear, reliable and effective communication.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the programme in designing assessment

statements.appliesTo: assessment in the subject
statements.about: transparency where technology is used in assessment
statements.paraphrase: Authentic assessment, fresh examples and personal experience promote academic integrity, and students respond to others' work rather than report it; any use of technology in assessment must be transparent; self and peer assessment with clear marking criteria support learning.

forPractitioner.text: Make any use of technology in assessment transparent, which the paragraph makes a must; promote integrity through authentic tasks and personal examples, and give students self and peer assessment against clear criteria.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in how assessment uses technology

statements.appliesTo: providers awarding honours in the subject
statements.about: referring to Annex D for achievement above threshold
statements.paraphrase: Most students will go beyond the minimum threshold; each provider decides what counts as evidence of that and should refer to Annex D of the UK degree frameworks, which describes the four main honours classifications.

forPractitioner.text: Most students exceed the threshold; the provider decides what evidence shows this and should use Annex D of the 2024 UK degree frameworks, with its descriptions of the 1st, 2.1, 2.2 and 3rd classes.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in judging classifications

statements.appliesTo: providers that write competence standards
statements.paraphrase: The three rungs, for undergraduate and master's study alike, do not set universal competence standards; a provider that develops competence standards under the Equality Act 2010 may draw on the statement and any PSRB requirements, and should then follow the latest Equality and Human Rights Commission guidance.

forPractitioner.text: Do not treat the rungs as competence standards; if you write competence standards into a programme specification under the Equality Act 2010, draw on this statement and any PSRB requirements and follow the latest EHRC guidance.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in writing competence standards

statements.appliesTo: students completing any philosophy module
statements.about: competence expected from any philosophy module
statements.paraphrase: Philosophy is studied in single and joint honours and within modular degrees; the rung descriptions are meant for single honours, and what is expected of students taking less philosophy scales accordingly; anyone completing a philosophy module is expected to have some general philosophical skills and to know the texts and topics in its description.

forPractitioner.text: Write the rung descriptions into single honours outcomes; for joint, modular and elective students scale the expectations, but anyone finishing a philosophy module is expected to show some general philosophical skills and knowledge of the module's texts and topics.

forBeneficiary.text: If you complete any philosophy module, you are expected to have some general philosophical skills and to know the texts and topics the module describes.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will know and understand the work of a number of major philosophers, as set down in their own texts.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show knowledge and understanding of the texts of several of the great philosophers.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will know and understand what several major philosophers wrote.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: an original interpretation from close reading
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will know major philosophers' theories, arguments and interpretative disputes and will offer a reading of their own grounded in close study of the original texts.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will add to knowledge of the theories and the interpretative debates an original interpretation of their own, built on close reading of the primary sources.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will also put forward your own original reading of the philosophers you study, based on close attention to what they actually wrote.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: theories of major philosophers and the disputes over reading them
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will know the theories and arguments of major philosophers, met in the original texts, together with the main disputes over how to read them.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will understand major philosophers' theories and arguments from their own texts and the key debates about how those texts are interpreted.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will know the main theories and arguments of major philosophers from reading them directly, and where scholars disagree about how to read them.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: core theories in logic, metaphysics, epistemology or mind
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will know some core theories and arguments from logic, epistemology, metaphysics or the philosophy of mind, each taken in a wide sense.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand some of the principal theories and arguments in theoretical philosophy: logic, epistemology, metaphysics or the philosophy of mind.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will know some of the main theories and arguments about logic, knowledge, reality or the mind.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: systematic, comparative command of theoretical philosophy
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will know many theories and arguments in logic, epistemology, metaphysics or the philosophy of mind, systematically, widely and by comparison, possibly reaching past what they were taught.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will command many theories and arguments in theoretical philosophy, compare them systematically and may show knowledge beyond the taught curriculum.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will know many theories and arguments about logic, knowledge, reality or the mind, compare them carefully and often go beyond what your course covered.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: more of the core theories in theoretical philosophy
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will know a wider share of the core theories and arguments in logic, epistemology, metaphysics or the philosophy of mind.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will understand more of the principal theories and arguments in theoretical philosophy than the threshold asks.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will know more of the main theories and arguments about logic, knowledge, reality or the mind.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: core theories in moral, political or social philosophy
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will know some core theories and arguments in ethics, political philosophy or social philosophy, each in a wide sense.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand some principal theories and arguments in practical philosophy: moral, political or social.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will know some of the main theories and arguments about ethics, politics or society.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: systematic, comparative command of practical philosophy
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will know many theories and arguments in ethics, political or social philosophy, systematically, widely and by comparison, possibly reaching past what they were taught.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will command many theories and arguments in practical philosophy, compare them systematically and may show knowledge beyond the taught curriculum.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will know many theories and arguments about ethics, politics or society, compare them carefully and often go beyond what your course covered.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: more of the core theories in practical philosophy
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will know a wider share of the core theories and arguments in ethics, political philosophy or social philosophy.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will understand more of the principal theories and arguments in practical philosophy than the threshold asks.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will know more of the main theories and arguments about ethics, politics or society.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: a few techniques of philosophical reasoning
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will know a narrow set of methods of philosophical reasoning.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will understand a small number of techniques of philosophical reasoning.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will know a few of the methods philosophers use to reason.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: an extensive repertoire and the debates over method
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will know a wide array of reasoning techniques together with the critiques of, and debates over, philosophical method.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will understand an extensive repertoire of reasoning techniques and the critiques and debates surrounding philosophical method.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will know a wide range of reasoning methods and the arguments about how philosophy should be done.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: wider techniques and critiques of method
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will know a wider set of reasoning techniques and the philosophical criticisms made of philosophy's own methods.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will understand a wider range of reasoning techniques and how philosophers have criticised the discipline's methods.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will know more reasoning methods and how philosophers have questioned the methods of philosophy itself.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will know some of the leading open questions in present-day philosophical debate and research.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be aware of some major issues in current philosophical research.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will know some of the big questions philosophers are debating and researching now.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: current issues assessed from close reading, beyond the taught
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will know and critically assess many leading current questions, working from close reading of the primary literature and possibly beyond what was taught.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will assess many current research issues critically from close reading of primary sources, often reaching past the taught material.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will judge many current debates critically from your own close reading of the original texts, often going beyond your course.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will know many of the leading current questions in philosophy and will be able to assess them critically.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will know many major issues in current research and assess them critically.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will know many of the big questions in current philosophy and be able to judge them critically.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will choose readings and primary sources and comment on them.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will select readings and primary texts and offer comment on them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will pick suitable readings and original sources and say something useful about them.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will critically evaluate and bring together a wide body of readings and primary sources, drawing in material from other branches or traditions of philosophy or from other subjects.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will critically evaluate and synthesise wide reading, using relevant work from other subfields, other traditions or other disciplines.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will critically assess and pull together a wide range of reading, including relevant work from other parts of philosophy or other subjects.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: evaluating readings, sometimes beyond the list
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will choose, comment on and evaluate readings and primary sources, at times going past the set list.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will select, comment on and evaluate readings and primary texts, sometimes from outside the reading list.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will choose, comment on and assess readings and original sources, sometimes going beyond your reading list.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will understand why interpreting texts matters.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will grasp why textual interpretation matters in philosophy.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will understand why the way you interpret a text matters.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: sophisticated interpretation across eras and traditions
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will draw sophisticated readings across periods and traditions and critically examine their foundations and wider philosophical consequences with great clarity and insight.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will produce sophisticated interpretations spanning periods and traditions and examine critically what they rest on and imply, with exceptional clarity.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will offer sophisticated readings across periods and traditions and examine clearly and insightfully what they rest on and what they imply.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: contextual reading and rigorous assessment of textual arguments
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will read and interpret texts from different periods or traditions with attention to context, pick out the arguments in them and test their structure and consequences rigorously.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will interpret texts from various periods or traditions in context, identify their arguments and rigorously assess how those arguments are built and what follows from them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will read texts from different times and traditions carefully and in context, find the arguments in them and test how they work and what follows.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will use the technical vocabulary of philosophy correctly.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will use philosophical terms accurately.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will use philosophical terms correctly.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: precise use and new terms where apt
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will use general and specialist philosophical vocabulary precisely and, where it helps, coin new terms.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will handle both general and specialist terms precisely and introduce new terms where the argument needs them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will use general and specialist terms precisely and, when it helps your argument, introduce new terms of your own.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will use philosophical vocabulary with precision, some specialist terms included.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will use philosophical terms precisely, including some specialist ones.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will use philosophical terms precisely, including some specialist ones.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: presenting an argument, aware of soundness
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will put forward an argument and show they know what makes an argument sound.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will present an argument and show awareness of what soundness requires.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will make an argument and show that you know what makes an argument sound.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will construct subtle arguments precisely and rigorously, reaching well-supported conclusions from sound reasoning and a full grasp of the relevant concepts and theories, with depth, clarity and keen awareness of complexity and consequence.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will produce precise, rigorous and nuanced arguments whose well-justified conclusions rest on sound reasoning and thorough command of the concepts and theories, aware of their complexities and implications.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will build subtle, precise and rigorous arguments, reach well-supported conclusions and show a deep, clear sense of the complications and consequences involved.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will build arguments with care, draw only conclusions the premises support, anticipate objections and defend against them.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will formulate arguments scrupulously, draw only justified conclusions, foresee objections and answer them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will build arguments carefully, claim only what your reasons support, foresee objections and answer them.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will explain complicated matters and ideas.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will explain complex issues and ideas.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will explain complicated ideas.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will adapt their explanations to different audiences without oversimplifying.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will fit explanations to varied audiences while avoiding oversimplification.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will adjust your explanations to suit different audiences without making the ideas too simple.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: clear explanation, apt simplification and examples
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will explain complex matters and ideas clearly, simplify them where fitting and illustrate them with useful examples.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will explain complex ideas clearly, simplify them appropriately and illustrate them with good examples.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will explain complex ideas clearly, simplify them when that helps and use good examples.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will show a little originality.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show some modest originality.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will show some ideas of your own.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: original, plausible lines of argument in depth
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will work out original and plausible lines of argument in depth.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will develop original, plausible lines of argument in depth.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will develop original and convincing lines of argument in depth.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will work out some ideas and arguments of their own.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will develop some original ideas and arguments.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will develop some ideas and arguments of your own.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: strengths and weaknesses on both sides
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will pick out what is strong and weak in the arguments on each side of a philosophical question.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will identify strengths and weaknesses in arguments on both sides of a question.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will spot the strong and weak points in the arguments on each side of a philosophical question.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: suspending judgement and revising firm views
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will hold back judgement, meet new perspectives with open curiosity and have the honesty to revise even firm convictions when the case requires it.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will suspend judgement, approach new perspectives with curiosity and honestly revise strongly held views where warranted.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will hold off judging, explore new perspectives with curiosity and honestly change even firmly held beliefs when the arguments call for it.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will consider unfamiliar ideas openly and be ready to change their minds when that is warranted.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will review unfamiliar ideas openly and change their minds where appropriate.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will consider new ideas with an open mind and be willing to change your view when you should.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will name some ways philosophy and other disciplines can shape each other.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will identify some ways in which philosophy feeds into, and draws on, other disciplines.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will point to some ways philosophy and other subjects learn from each other.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: critiquing philosophy in other fields and the reverse
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will describe, explain and critique the philosophical assumptions at work in other fields and see how ideas and research from outside philosophy bear on its debates.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will analyse and critique philosophical doctrines embedded in work from other disciplines and recognise what outside ideas and research contribute to philosophical debate.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will find and critique the philosophical ideas inside work from other subjects, and see how research from those subjects matters to philosophical debates.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will describe and explain some ways philosophy and other disciplines shape each other.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will describe and explain some of the two-way links between philosophy and other disciplines.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will describe and explain some ways philosophy and other subjects learn from each other.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, graduates will say how philosophy can bear on some everyday concerns.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will state some ways philosophy connects with ordinary life.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will say how philosophy can connect with some everyday concerns.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the excellent level
statements.about: applying philosophy to real problems and dilemmas
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, graduates will show a subtle understanding of how philosophy matters to lived experience, using its insights to clarify and tackle real-world complexity and ethical dilemmas.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will apply philosophical insight with nuance to everyday experience, shedding light on real problems and ethical dilemmas and helping to address them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will show a subtle grasp of how philosophy matters to daily life and use it to shed light on real problems and ethical dilemmas.

statements.appliesTo: single honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Typically, graduates will describe and explain some ways philosophy bears on everyday concerns.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will describe and explain some connections between philosophy and ordinary life.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will describe and explain some ways philosophy connects with everyday concerns.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to recognise the issues, questions and problems a topic raises.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will identify the issues, questions and problems a topic raises.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to spot the issues, questions and problems a topic raises.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.about: finding and filling gaps in knowledge
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to see where their own knowledge falls short and learn what is missing.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will identify gaps in what they know and acquire the knowledge to fill them.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to see what you do not yet know and go and learn it.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to grasp and break down knowledge and information.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand and analyse the knowledge and information they meet.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to understand and analyse the knowledge and information you come across.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to draw together what is known on a given topic.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will synthesise the current state of knowledge on a topic.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to pull together what is currently known about a topic.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to use knowledge and understanding to reach conclusions backed by evidence.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will apply knowledge and understanding to reach conclusions supported by evidence.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to use what you know to reach conclusions backed by evidence.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.about: communicating in speech or other forms
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to communicate well and fittingly, in speech or by other means.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will communicate effectively and appropriately, verbally, non-verbally or both.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to communicate well and appropriately, in speech or in other forms.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.about: presenting knowledge or arguments to others
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to set out knowledge or an argument so that others can follow it.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will present knowledge or an argument in a form others can understand.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to set out what you know, or an argument, so other people can follow it.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to use a range of digital technologies critically to gather, analyse, choose and present information.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will engage critically with varied digital tools to collate, analyse, select and present information.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to use different digital tools critically to gather, analyse, choose and present information.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show intellectual independence: working alone with suitable guidance and support, researching on their own initiative and judging critically.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will assert intellectual independence by working independently with fitting guidance, carrying out self-directed research and exercising critical judgement.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to think for yourself: work on your own with the right support, carry out your own research and make critical judgements.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to work with others, in a group or team or by taking part in discussion.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will work collaboratively, through group or team work, discussion or both.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to work with others, in a group or team or by joining in discussions.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.about: reflecting on progress and academic integrity
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to reflect on how they are progressing, academic integrity included.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will reflect on their own progress, including matters of academic integrity.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to reflect on your own progress, including how you keep your work honest and properly referenced.

statements.appliesTo: undergraduate graduates of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to recognise and examine the values and ethics beneath culture and society and in their own lives.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will identify and examine the values and ethics underlying culture, society and personal life.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to recognise and question the values and ethics behind culture, society and your own life.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.about: comprehensive understanding informed by current research
statements.paraphrase: Will show a sophisticated, thorough understanding of the discipline's key concepts, theories, issues and debates, shaped by current research and advanced scholarship.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will understand the key concepts, theories, issues and debates of philosophy in a sophisticated and comprehensive way, shaped by current research.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand the main concepts, theories, issues and debates in philosophy in depth and breadth, shaped by current research.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will show knowledge of suitable research methods and use fitting research skills.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will know which research methods suit their work and will apply the research skills it needs.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know which research methods suit your work and use the research skills it calls for.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.about: advanced analysis of arguments and texts
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to construct, assess and critically analyse demanding arguments, texts, positions and problems in philosophy at an advanced standard, with rigorous method.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will construct, evaluate and critically analyse demanding philosophical arguments, texts and problems at an advanced standard, with rigorous method.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to build, assess and critically analyse difficult philosophical arguments, texts and problems at an advanced level, using rigorous methods.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will show expertise in at least one specialist area or tradition, gained through deep study and research.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will have expert knowledge of one or more specialist areas or traditions from in-depth study and research.

forBeneficiary.text: You will become expert in one or more specialist areas or traditions of philosophy through deep study and research.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will show the capacity to conceive, plan and carry out a sustained piece of philosophical research that adds to the field.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will conceive, design and complete a substantial philosophical research project that makes a contribution to the field.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to plan, design and complete a substantial philosophical research project that adds something to your field.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will show well-developed skill in rational and logical analysis, in interpreting complex ideas and in building sophisticated arguments and chains of reasoning.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will analyse rationally and logically, interpret complex ideas and construct sophisticated reasoning at a highly developed level.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be highly skilled at logical analysis, at interpreting complex ideas and at building sophisticated arguments.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will show an appreciation of what philosophical ideas mean beyond philosophy, for other disciplines and for real situations.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will appreciate the wider significance of philosophical ideas for other disciplines and for real-world settings.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand why philosophical ideas matter beyond philosophy, for other subjects and in real situations.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.about: communicating complex ideas to all audiences
statements.paraphrase: Will show advanced writing and presentation skills, spoken or otherwise, that convey complex ideas well to specialists and non-specialists.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will write and present at an advanced level, conveying complex ideas effectively to specialist and general audiences.

forBeneficiary.text: You will write and present at an advanced level, getting complex ideas across to experts and non-experts.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will show the ability to take part in long philosophical dialogue, debate and shared inquiry.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will sustain philosophical dialogue, debate and collaborative inquiry.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to keep up philosophical discussion, debate and shared inquiry with others over time.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will show a reflective grasp of what philosophy is as a discipline, its methods and assumptions, and how it relates to other kinds of inquiry.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will reflect on the nature of philosophy, its methods and presuppositions and its relation to other inquiry.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand, reflectively, what philosophy is, how it works, what it assumes and how it relates to other kinds of inquiry.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.about: ethical reasoning and philosophy's social role
statements.paraphrase: Will show skill in ethical reasoning and an appreciation of the moral side of philosophical problems and of philosophy's part in tackling ethical, social and political issues.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will reason ethically and appreciate both the moral dimensions of philosophical problems and philosophy's role in ethical, social and political questions.

forBeneficiary.text: You will reason well about ethics and see the moral side of philosophical problems and how philosophy can help with ethical, social and political issues.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will show the independent learning and research skills to find, assess and combine relevant sources and to keep developing as a philosopher.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates will learn and research independently, identifying, evaluating and synthesising sources and continuing their philosophical development.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to learn and research on your own, finding, assessing and combining sources, and keep growing as a philosopher.
